options.label: 1. Your Phone Motion Sensor Is Reading Your Passwords
options.detail:
Demonstrates how mobile websites read motion sensors without permission to decode keypresses via vibration physics, prompting viewers to check their browser permission settings immediately.
Hook (en): Your phone knows what you type before you hit send.
Why: Recent cybersecurity alerts highlight that mobile gyroscopes and accelerometers can infer PINs and keystrokes with over 80% accuracy without triggering OS permission popups, driving massive paranoia and immediate verification comments.

options.label: 2. The 1-Second Clipboard Trap Exposing Snooping Apps
options.detail:
Guides the viewer through a real-time live test copying a burner phrase to expose which background apps silently read their clipboard every time they launch.
Hook (en): Copy this exact word right now.
Why: Clipboard hijacking and background paste access remain top-tier viral privacy concerns; viewers love interactive commands where their screen gives immediate visual feedback (e.g., paste notifications).

options.label: 3. The 5-Second Blink Glitch Exposing AI Deepfakes
options.detail:
Shows a lightning-fast visual trick to spot real-time AI face-swappers during video calls by forcing them to turn sideways or counting abnormal blink intervals.
Hook (en): Look closely at their eyes right now.
Why: Surging real-time deepfake video scams on FaceTime and WhatsApp have made biometric verification tips go hyper-viral across social media platforms.
